about.title: Los Alamitos Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a car part gives out on Katella Avenue, a tool malfunctions in a Los Alamitos garage, or a household item breaks in a way it never should have. Whatever the setting, the injuries are real and the recovery can be slow. California law generally lets injured people pursue manufacturers, distributors, and retailers under strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective, not on proving anyone was careless. That's a meaningful advantage for someone in Los Alamitos trying to piece together what happened after an injury. We handle product liability claims directly and charge no fee unless you recover. If we take your case, we work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to you. The first step is simply finding out whether your situation fits a product liability claim, and that conversation is free and confidential.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters for Los Alamitos Residents

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, the focus stays on the product's flaw rather than proving the manufacturer was careless. That can make a real difference for someone still recovering from an injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California law. Our team can help sort out who was involved in getting the product to you.

items.title: Preserving the Product Preserves Your Claim
items.desc: Keeping the item, its packaging, and any related receipts intact is often critical to a product liability case. We can advise you early on how to protect that evidence.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, which means showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from a general negligence claim, and we can explain how it applies to your situation.

items.question: What if the product broke and I no longer have it?
items.answer: It's still worth having a conversation with us, but keeping the product, even in damaged condition, is usually very helpful to a claim. If you still have it, don't repair, discard, or alter it before speaking with our team.

items.question: Is this only about car accidents on Katella Avenue or I-605?
items.answer: No — product liability covers defective items themselves, not the roads where an incident might happen. Whether the product failed while driving near Cerritos Avenue, at home, or at work in Los Alamitos, the defect is what matters for this type of claim.

items.question: Does your firm charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. We provide free case reviews and don't charge you upfront. If we take your case, we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
